stories.title: EU calls emergency meeting to discuss Ceuta migrant crossings
stories.body: There have been tense exchanges between Spain and other EU states over the influx of migrants into the enclave of Ceuta.

stories.title: Call for 'full review' as pressure grows on Infantino
stories.body: The leadership of Fifa is publicly questioned by football's governing bodies in Europe, North and Central America and the Caribbean.

stories.title: Tourist plane crashes in Peru, killing 13
stories.body: The small plane was flying over the Nazca Lines ​archaeological site when it crashed, according to local reports.

stories.title: Israeli West Bank settler tells BBC attacks on Palestinians are justified as revenge
stories.body: Settler violence against Palestinians is on the rise in the West Bank, as settlements and outposts expand.

stories.title: Italy putting nearly all major cities on highest heat alert
stories.body: Some 19 major Italian cities - including Rome, Milan and Naples - are already on red alert, and by Monday all but two will be.

stories.title: Mountaineer Nirmal Purja killed in Pakistan avalanche, his company says
stories.body: The renowned mountaineer was known for scaling the world's 14 highest peaks in just over six months in 2019.

stories.title: Current Ebola outbreak worst ever in DR Congo, WHO says
stories.body: The current strain has so far killed 1,587 people, and there is currently no approved vaccine or treatment.

stories.title: Three killed after woman detonates bomb at Moscow restaurant, state media say
stories.body: Security officials said the female attacker tried to enter the restaurant but was stopped by a security guard.

stories.title: Nine killed in strikes on Kyiv, as Ukraine sinks Russian container ship
stories.body: The attack comes as Moscow escalates deadly ballistic missile attacks on the Ukrainian capital.

stories.title: Peru's ex-president leaves jail after 15-year jail term for corruption overturned
stories.body: Ollanta Humala had been convicted of money laundering offences alongside his wife in 2025.

stories.title: India's 'cockroach' protesters have wounds consistent with pellet-gun fire, say experts
stories.body: Ballistic experts say the dozens of tiny round punctures are tell-tale signs of pellet gun injuries.

stories.title: Trump administration drops Reflecting Pool vandalism charge and admits 'botched' repairs
stories.body: President Donald Trump had blamed "sick" vandals, and a former Olympian had been charged, but prosecutors now say contractors caused the damage.

stories.title: UK rapper Yung Filly found not guilty of raping woman after Australian show
stories.body: The YouTuber has been found guilty for two counts of assault over the 2024 incident in Perth.

stories.title: Danube's record low levels force shutdown of Hungary's only nuclear plant
stories.body: Romania, Bulgaria and Serbia are also grappling with the effects of a series of prolonged heatwaves and low rainfall.

stories.title: Death row inmates desperate to escape execution in Saudi Arabia call the BBC
stories.body: Dozens of Ethiopians are awaiting execution - some called the BBC to tell their stories.

stories.title: Infantino on the brink? Who might replace him if he goes?
stories.body: Fifa president Gianni Infantino is in the eye of a storm after scrapping his attempt to sell stakes in the World Cup. If he goes, who comes in?

stories.title: Bowen: Plan for Hamas to disarm faces big obstacles, yet it offers rare hope for Gaza
stories.body: The realities of politics, war, zero trust, the deaths of thousands and the destruction of Gaza will make any agreement very complicated.

stories.title: Chelsea was murdered 10 years ago - will a new police podcast catch her killer?
stories.body: More police departments are trying to invigorate unsolved murder or missing cases through the power of podcasts.

stories.title: Greyhounds bound for Australia as New Zealand racing ban takes effect
stories.body: At least two chartered flights carrying up to 150 greyhounds are set to fly to Australia's eastern states, the BBC understands.

stories.title: Why limited war with the US may suit Iran better than peace
stories.body: Iran may believe it can control its conflict carefully enough to keep pressure on the US while avoiding an all-out war.
